questions.text: Two guns A and B can fire bullets at speeds 1 km/s and 2 km/s respectively. From a point on a horizontal ground, they are fired in all possible directions. The ratio of maximum areas covered by the bullets fired by the two guns, on the ground is -

questions.text: Two forces P and Q, of magnitude 2F and 3F, respectively, are at an angle theta with each other. If the force Q is doubled, then their resultant also gets doubled. Then, the angle theta is -

If R2 = 2R1

questions.text: A shell is fired from a fixed artillery gun with an initial speed u such that it hits the target on the ground at a distance R from it. If t1 and t2 are the values of the time taken by it to hit the target in two possible ways, the product t1t2 is -

=> t1t2 = (4u^2 sin theta cos theta)/g^2 = (2u^2 (sin 2theta))/g = (2/g)((u^2 sin 2theta)/g) = (2R)/g

questions.text: The trajectory of a projectile near the surface of the earth is given as y = 2x - 9x^2. If it were launched at an angle θ_0 with speed v_0 then (g = 10 ms^(-2)):
questions.sol_text:
The trajectory equation for a projectile is:
y = x tan θ (1 - x/R) ......(i)

Given equation of trajectory: y = 2x - 9x^2 = 2x(1 - 9x/2) = 2x(1 - x/(2/9)) ......(2)

Comparing equations (1) & (2):
tan θ = 2 & R = 2/9

From the right triangle with opposite = 2, adjacent = 1, hypotenuse = sqrt(5):
cos θ = 1/sqrt(5) ⟹ θ = cos^(-1)(1/sqrt(5))

From R = v_0^2 sin(2θ)/g:
⟹ v_0^2 sin(2θ)/g = 2/9

Using sin(2θ) = 2 tan θ/(1 + tan^2 θ):
⟹ v_0^2 [2 tan θ/(1 + tan^2 θ)]/10 = 2/9

⟹ v_0^2 [4/5]/10 = 2/9

⟹ v_0^2 [4/5] = (2/9) × 10

⟹ v_0^2 = (2 × 10 × 5)/(9 × 4)

⟹ v_0^2 = 100/36

⟹ v_0 = 10/6 = 5/3 ms^(-1)

questions.text: Two particles A, B are moving on two concentric circles of radii R1 and R2 with equal angular speed omega. At t = 0, their positions and direction of motion are shown in the figure. The relative velocity vector_v_A - vector_v_B at t = pi/(2omega) is given by:
questions.sol_text:
T = 2pi/omega

theta = omega*t

= omega * 2pi/(2omega)

At t = pi/(2omega):

theta = omega * pi/(2omega) = pi/2

From the diagram at theta = pi/2:

vector_v_A = -R1*omega*i

vector_v_B = R2*omega*i

Therefore:
vector_v_A - vector_v_B = -R1*omega*i - R2*omega*i

= -omega(R1 + R2)*i

Wait, rechecking the directions at theta = pi/2:

Particle A starts at angle 0 (on positive x-axis) moving counterclockwise (upward in +y direction)
Particle B starts at angle -pi/2 (on negative y-axis) moving clockwise (downward in -y direction)

At t = pi/(2omega), theta = pi/2:

Particle A has rotated pi/2, so it's at angle pi/2 (top of circle), velocity is in -x direction: vector_v_A = -R1*omega*i

Particle B has rotated pi/2 clockwise from -pi/2, so it's at angle -pi/2 + pi/2 = 0 (on positive x-axis), velocity is in +y direction (from clockwise motion at that point): Actually, for clockwise motion at angle 0, velocity is in -y direction.

Rechecking initial conditions and directions more carefully from the figure description and solution:

vector_v_A = -R1*omega*i (at t = pi/(2omega))

vector_v_B = R2*omega*i (at t = pi/(2omega))

vector_v_A - vector_v_B = omega(R2 - R1)*i

questions.text: Let |vector A₁| = 3, |vector A₂| = 5 and |vector A₁ + vector A₂| = 5. The value of (2vector A₁ + 3vector A₂) • (3vector A₁ - 2vector A₂) is -
questions.sol_text:
(2vector A₁ + 3vector A₂) • (3vector A₁ - 2vector A₂)
= 6vector A₁² - 4vector A₁ • vector A₂ + 9vector A₁ • vector A₂ - 6vector A₂²
= 6(vector A₁² - vector A₂²) + 5vector A₁ • vector A₂ cos(theta)
= 6(9 - 25) + 5vector A₁vector A₂ cos(theta)
= -96 + 5vector A₁vector A₂ cos(theta)

Using |vector A₁ + vector A₂|² = vector A₁² + vector A₂² + 2vector A₁vector A₂ cos(theta):
25 = 9 + 25 + 2vector A₁vector A₂ cos(theta)
25 = 34 + 2vector A₁vector A₂ cos(theta)
vector A₁vector A₂ cos(theta) = -9/2

= -96 + 5 × (-9/2)
= -96 - 45/2
= -118.5

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Ship A is sailing towards north-east with velocity vector v = 30i + 50j km/hr where i points east and j points north. Ship B is at a distance of 80 km east and 150 km north of Ship A and is sailing towards west at 10 km/hr. A will be at minimum distance from B in -
questions.sol_text:
Let us set up a coordinate system with Ship A at the origin at t = 0.

Velocity of Ship A: vector v_A = 30i + 50j km/hr
Initial position of Ship B relative to A: vector r_BA = 80i + 150j km
Velocity of Ship B: vector v_B = -10i km/hr (sailing west)

Relative velocity of A with respect to B:
vector v_AB = vector v_A - vector v_B = (30i + 50j) - (-10i) = 40i + 50j km/hr

The position of A relative to B at time t:
vector r_AB(t) = vector r_BA + vector v_AB * t = 80i + 150j + (40i + 50j)t

Wait, let me reconsider. The initial position of B relative to A is:
vector r_BA(0) = 80i + 150j km

The relative velocity of A with respect to B:
vector v_AB = vector v_A - vector v_B = (30i + 50j) - (-10i) = 40i + 50j km/hr

Position of A relative to B at time t:
vector r_AB(t) = vector r_BA(0) - vector v_AB * t
Actually, the relative position vector from B to A is:
vector r_AB(t) = 80i + 150j - (40i + 50j)t

No, let me use the correct approach:
The relative velocity of A with respect to B: vector v_AB = vector v_A - vector v_B = 40i + 50j
Initial position vector from A to B: vector r_BA(0) = 80i + 150j

For minimum distance, we use:
t_min = -(vector v_AB · vector r_BA) / |vector v_AB|^2

vector v_AB · vector r_BA = (40i + 50j) · (80i + 150j) = 40(80) + 50(150) = 3200 + 7500 = 10700

|vector v_AB|^2 = 40^2 + 50^2 = 1600 + 2500 = 4100

t_min = -10700 / 4100 = -2.61 hrs

Since we get a negative value, let me reconsider the sign convention.

The correct formula is: t_min = (vector v_AB · vector r_BA) / |vector v_AB|^2

But vector r_BA should be from B to A initially, which is opposite:
vector r_BA(0) = -80i - 150j (position of A relative to B)

Actually, the position of B relative to A is 80i + 150j, so position of A relative to B is -80i - 150j.

vector v_AB · vector r_AB = (40i + 50j) · (-80i - 150j) = -3200 - 7500 = -10700

t_min = |vector v_AB · vector r_AB| / |vector v_AB|^2 = 10700 / 4100 = 2.61 hrs ≈ 2.6 hrs

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The stream of a river is flowing with a speed of 2 km/h. A swimmer can swim at a speed of 4 km/h. What should be the direction of the swimmer with respect to the flow of the river to cross the river straight?
questions.sol_text:
Let V_r = velocity of river = 2 km/h (along the flow)
Let V_m = velocity of swimmer = 4 km/h
Let theta = angle of swimmer's velocity with respect to perpendicular to river flow

For the swimmer to cross the river straight, the resultant velocity should be perpendicular to the river banks (i.e., perpendicular to the flow).

The component of swimmer's velocity along the river flow must cancel out the river's velocity:
V_m sin(theta) = V_r
4 sin(theta) = 2
sin(theta) = 1/2
theta = 30°

This means the swimmer must swim at an angle of 30° to the perpendicular direction (or 30° upstream from the perpendicular).

The angle with respect to the river flow direction is measured as:
Angle from river flow = 90° + 30° = 120°

Therefore, the swimmer should swim at 120° with respect to the flow of the river.

questions.text: The position co-ordinates of a particle moving in a 3-D coordinate system is given by x = a cos(ωt), y = a sin(ωt) and z = aωt. The speed of the particle is:

Using sin^2(ωt) + cos^2(ωt) = 1:

|V| = sqrt(a^2 ω^2 + a^2 ω^2)

|V| = sqrt(2a^2 ω^2)

questions.text: The sum of two forces P and Q is R such that |R| = |P|. The angle theta (in degrees) that the resultant of 2P and Q will make with Q is, .............
questions.sol_text:
Given: vector P + vector Q = vector R and |R| = |P|

From vector addition:
vector P + vector Q = vector R

Taking magnitude squared:
|P|^2 + |Q|^2 + 2|P||Q|cos(theta) = |R|^2 = |P|^2

Simplifying:
|Q|^2 + 2|P||Q|cos(theta) = 0
2|P|cos(theta) + |Q| = 0  ...(1)

For the resultant of 2P and Q, using tan(alpha) formula:
tan(alpha) = (2|P| sin(theta))/(2|P| cos(theta) + |Q|)  ...(2)

From equation (1): 2|P|cos(theta) + |Q| = 0

Substituting in equation (2):
tan(alpha) = (2|P| sin(theta))/0 = infinity

Therefore: alpha = 90°

questions.text: A clock has a continuously moving second's hand of 0.1 m length. The average acceleration of the tip of the hand (in units of ms^(-2)) is of the order of -
questions.sol_text:
R = 0.1 m

For a second's hand, period T = 60 seconds

Angular velocity:
ω = 2π/T = 2π/60 = 0.105 rad/sec

For circular motion, the centripetal acceleration at the tip of the hand is:
a = ω²R

Substituting values:
a = (0.105)² × (0.1)
a = 0.01105 × 0.1
a = 0.0011
a = 1.1 × 10^(-3) ms^(-2)

Therefore, the average acceleration is of the order of 10^(-3) ms^(-2).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: When a car is at rest, its driver sees rain drops falling on it vertically. When driving the car with speed v, he sees that rain drops are coming at an angle 60° from the horizontal. On further increasing the speed of the car to (1 + β)v, this angle changes to 45°. The value of β is close to:
questions.sol_text:
Rain is falling vertically downwards.

vector_r/m = vector_r - vector_m

At speed v:
tan 60° = v_r / v_m = sqrt(3)

v_r = v_m * sqrt(3) = v * sqrt(3)

Now, v_m = (1 + β)v
and θ = 45°

tan 45° = v_r / v_m = 1

v_r = v_m

sqrt(3) = 1 + β

⟹ β = sqrt(3) - 1 = 0.73

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A particle (m = 1 kg) slides down a frictionless track (AOC) starting from rest at a point A (height 2 m). After reaching C, the particle continues to move freely in air as a projectile. When it reaching its highest point P (height 1 m), the kinetic energy of the particle (in J) is: (Figure drawn is schematic and not to scale; take g = 10 m s^(-2))
questions.sol_text:
Using conservation of energy:

At point A:
- Height = 2 m
- Velocity = 0 (starts from rest)
- Total mechanical energy = mgh = 1 × 10 × 2 = 20 J

At highest point P:
- Height = 1 m
- The particle is moving as a projectile
- At the highest point, the vertical component of velocity is zero
- Only horizontal component of velocity remains

Using conservation of energy from A to P:
Total energy at A = Total energy at P
mgh_A = mgh_P + (1/2)mv_P^2

1 × 10 × 2 = 1 × 10 × 1 + (1/2) × 1 × v_P^2

20 = 10 + (1/2)v_P^2

10 = (1/2)v_P^2

Kinetic energy at P = (1/2)mv_P^2 = 10 J

Alternatively:
K.E. = ΔP.E. = mgh = 1 × 10 × 1 = 10 Joule

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A particle moves such that its position vector r(t) = cos(ωt) i + sin(ωt) j where ω is a constant and t is time. Then which of the following statements is true for the velocity v(t) and acceleration a(t) of the particle:
options: v and a both are perpendicular to r
v is perpendicular to r and a is directed towards the origin
v and a both are parallel to r
v is perpendicular to r and a is directed away from the origin
questions.sol_text:
r = cos(ωt) i + sin(ωt) j

v = dr/dt = -ω sin(ωt) i + ω cos(ωt) j

a = dv/dt = -ω^2 cos(ωt) i - ω^2 sin(ωt) j
    = -ω^2(cos(ωt) i + sin(ωt) j)
    = -ω^2 r

v · r = (-ω sin(ωt) i + ω cos(ωt) j) · (cos(ωt) i + sin(ωt) j)
      = -ω sin(ωt) cos(ωt) + ω cos(ωt) sin(ωt)
      = 0 ⟹ v ⊥ r

Since, a = -ω^2 r
It is towards the origin

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A particle starts from the origin at t = 0 with an initial velocity of 3.0 i m/s and moves in the x-y plane with a constant acceleration (6.0 i + 4.0 j) m/s^2. The x-coordinate of the particle at the instant when its y-coordinate is 32 m is D metres. The value of D is -
questions.sol_text:
Given:
Initial velocity: vector u = 3 i m/s
Acceleration: vector a = 6 i + 4 j m/s^2
Y-coordinate when x-coordinate is D: y = 32 m

Using the equation of motion:
vector S = vector u t + (1/2) vector a t^2

For x-coordinate:
x = 3t + (1/2) × 6 t^2
x = 3t + 3t^2 .... (1)

For y-coordinate:
y = (1/2) × 4 × t^2 = 2t^2 = 32 (Given)

From y = 2t^2 = 32:
t^2 = 16
t = 4 sec .... (2)

Substituting t = 4 sec in equation (1):
x = 3 × 4 + 3 × 4^2
x = 12 + 3 × 16
x = 12 + 48
x = 60 m

Therefore, D = 60 metres

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A block of 200 g mass moves with a uniform speed in a horizontal circular groove, with vertical side walls of radius 20 cm. If the block takes 40 s to complete one round, the normal force by the side walls of the groove is:
questions.sol_text: Using centripetal force formula F = m*omega*R = m*(2*pi/T)*R. Given: m = 0.2 kg, R = 0.2 m, T = 40 s. F = 0.2 × (2*pi/40) × 0.2 = 0.2 × 4*pi × 0.2/40 = 9.859 × 10^-3 N. The normal force provides the centripetal force needed for circular motion.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A modern grand-prix racing car of mass m is traveling on a flat track in a circular arc of radius R with a speed u. If the coefficient of static friction between the tyres and the track is μ_s, then the magnitude of negative lift F_c acting downwards on the car is: (Assume forces on the four tyres are identical and g = acceleration due to gravity)
questions.sol_text: For circular motion, the centripetal force required is m*u^2/R. This is provided by friction force f_s = μ_s*N where N is the normal force. The normal force N = mg - F_c (since negative lift F_c acts downward, reducing the normal force). From f_s = μ_s*N = m*u^2/R, we get μ_s(mg - F_c) = m*u^2/R. Solving for F_c: F_c = m(g - u^2/(μ_s*R))

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A proton and an alpha particle, having kinetic energy K_p and K_a respectively, enter into a magnetic field at right angles. The ratio of the radii of trajectory of proton to that of alpha-particle is 2:1. The ratio of K_p : K_a is
questions.sol_text: Using the formula for radius of trajectory in magnetic field: R = mv/(qB) = sqrt(2mK)/(qB). For the ratio of kinetic energies: K_p/K_a = (2m_a/m_p) × (R_p/R_a)^2 × (q_a/q_p)^2. Given R_p/R_a = 2/1, m_a = 4m_p, q_a = 2q_p. Substituting: K_p/K_a = (2×4m_p/m_p) × (2)^2 × (2/1)^2 = 8 × 4 × (1/4) = 8 × 1 = 4:1

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A particle of mass m moves in a circular orbit under the central potential field V(r) = -C/r, where C is a constant. The correct radius-velocity graph of the particle's motion is:
options: Graph (A): Linear relationship between r and v starting from origin
Graph (B): Curved relationship showing r increasing with v, curve bending upward
Graph (C): Curved relationship showing r decreasing with v, hyperbolic decay
Graph (D): Curved relationship showing r and v with maximum point, then decreasing
questions.sol_text: For circular motion under central potential V(r) = -C/r, the effective potential is U = mV(r) = -Cm/r. The centripetal force is provided by F = -dU/dr = -Cm/r^2. For circular orbit: mv^2/r = Cm/r^2, which gives r = C/v^2, or equivalently v = sqrt(C/r). This means v is inversely proportional to sqrt(r), so as r increases, v decreases. The relationship is hyperbolic/curved with v decreasing as r increases, matching graph (C).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: If the angular velocity of earth's spin is increased such that the bodies at the equator start floating, the duration of the day would be approximately: [Take g = 10 m/s^2, the radius of earth, R = 6400 × 10^3 m, Take pi = 3.14]
questions.sol_text: At the equator, for bodies to float, the centripetal acceleration equals g. Using g_eff = g - omega^2*R = 0, we get omega = sqrt(g/R). The period T = 2*pi/omega = 2*pi*sqrt(R/g) = 2 × 3.14 × sqrt(6400×10^3/10) = 2 × 3.14 × 80 × 10 = 83.733 min ≈ 84 min.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The ranges and heights for two projectiles projected with the same initial velocity at angles 42° and 48° with the horizontal are R1, R2 and H1, H2 respectively. Choose the correct option:
questions.sol_text: Range R = u^2 sin(2θ)/g. For 42° and 48°: sin(2*42°) = sin(84°) and sin(2*48°) = sin(96°) = sin(84°), so R1 = R2. Maximum height H_max = u^2 sin^2(θ)/(2g). For 42°: H1 = u^2 sin^2(42°)/(2g). For 48°: H2 = u^2 sin^2(48°)/(2g). Since sin(48°) > sin(42°), we have H2 > H1, therefore H1 < H2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Two vectors P and Q have equal magnitudes. If the magnitude of P+Q is n times the magnitude of P-Q, then angle between P and Q is:
questions.sol_text: Let |P| = |Q| = x and angle between P and Q is theta. Given |P+Q| = n|P-Q|. Using magnitude formula: sqrt(x^2 + x^2 + 2x^2*cos(theta)) = n*sqrt(x^2 + x^2 - 2x^2*cos(theta)). Simplifying: sqrt(2x^2(1+cos(theta))) = n*sqrt(2x^2(1-cos(theta))). Squaring and dividing: (1+cos(theta))/(1-cos(theta)) = n^2. Solving: 1+cos(theta) = n^2(1-cos(theta)). Therefore: cos(theta) = (n^2-1)/(n^2+1). So theta = cos^(-1)((n^2-1)/(n^2+1)).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: If A and B are two vectors satisfying the relation A·B = |A×B|. Then the value of |A-B| will be:
questions.sol_text: Given: A·B = |A×B|. We know A·B = |A||B|cos(theta) and |A×B| = |A||B|sin(theta). So |A||B|cos(theta) = |A||B|sin(theta), which gives tan(theta) = 1, so theta = 45°. Now |A-B|^2 = A^2 + B^2 - 2A·B = A^2 + B^2 - 2|A||B|cos(45°) = A^2 + B^2 - 2AB·(1/sqrt(2)) = A^2 + B^2 - sqrt(2)AB. Therefore |A-B| = sqrt(A^2 + B^2 - sqrt(2)AB)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A butterfly is flying with a velocity 4√2 m/s in North - East direction. Wind is slowly blowing at 1 m/s from North to South. The resultant displacement of the butterfly in 3 seconds is:
questions.sol_text: Velocity of butterfly in North-East direction: v_bw = 4√2(cos(45°)i + sin(45°)j) = 4i + 4j m/s. Wind velocity from North to South: v_ws = 0i - j m/s. Resultant velocity: v_bj = v_bw + v_ws = (4i + 4j) + (0i - j) = 4i + 3j m/s. Speed of butterfly: |v_bj| = √(16 + 9) = √25 = 5 m/s. Displacement in 3 seconds: |displacement| = 5 × 3 = 15 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: What will be the projection of vector A = i + j + k on vector B = i + j ?
questions.sol_text: Component of A on B = (A · B)B / |B|^2. A · B = (i + j + k) · (i + j) = 1 + 1 + 0 = 2. |B|^2 = 1 + 1 = 2. Projection = (2/2)(i + j) = i + j.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: In an octagon ABCDEFGH of equal side, what is the sum of AB - AC - AD + AE + AF + AG + AH, if AO = 2i + 3j - 4k
questions.sol_text: Using vector properties with O as the center of the octagon: AB + AH = AO, AC + AG = 2AO, AD + AF = 3AO, AE = 2AO. Computing AB - AC - AD + AE + AF + AG + AH = AB + AH - (AC + AG) - (AD + AF) + AE + 2AO = AO - 2AO - 3AO + 2AO + 2AO = 8AO - 2AO - 3AO = AO + 2AO. After substitution and simplification: 16i - 24j + 32k

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Two vectors X and Y have equal magnitude. The magnitude of (X - Y) is n times the magnitude of (X + Y). The angle between X and Y is:
questions.sol_text: Given: |X| = |Y| and |X - Y| = n|X + Y|. Squaring: |X - Y|^2 = n^2|X + Y|^2. Expanding: X^2 + Y^2 - 2X·Y = n^2(X^2 + Y^2 + 2X·Y). Since |X| = |Y|, let |X|^2 = |Y|^2 = a. Then: 2a - 2X·Y = n^2(2a + 2X·Y). Simplifying: (1 - n^2)(2a) = (1 + n^2)(2X·Y). Therefore: X·Y = ((1 - n^2)/(1 + n^2))a. Since X·Y = |X||Y|cos(theta) = a·cos(theta), we get: cos(theta) = (1 - n^2)/(1 + n^2) = -(n^2 - 1)/(n^2 + 1). Thus: theta = cos^(-1)((n^2 - 1)/(-n^2 - 1))

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Match List I with List II. List I contains: (a) C - A - B = 0, (b) A - C - B = 0, (c) B - A - C = 0, (d) A + B = -C. List II contains four vector diagrams (i), (ii), (iii), (iv) showing triangle configurations with vectors A, B, and C. Choose the correct matching.
questions.sol_text: From triangle law of addition, we can clearly write answer. Analyzing each vector equation: (a) C - A - B = 0 means C = A + B (triangle law), (b) A - C - B = 0 means A = C + B, (c) B - A - C = 0 means B = A + C, (d) A + B = -C means A + B + C = 0. Matching with the vector diagrams based on the triangle law of vector addition and the orientation of vectors in each diagram.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The angle between vector (A) and (A - B) is:
options: tan^(-1)(B cos θ / (A - B sin θ))
questions.sol_text: Using the angle between vectors formula: tan(β) = B sin(60°) / (A - B cos(60°)). Since sin(60°) = sqrt(3)/2 and cos(60°) = 1/2, we get tan(β) = B(sqrt(3)/2) / (A - B/2) = sqrt(3)B / (2A - B). Therefore β = tan^(-1)(sqrt(3)B / (2A - B))

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A particle of mass m is suspended from a ceiling through a string of length L. The particle moves in a horizontal circle of radius r such that r = L/sqrt(2). The speed of particle will be:
questions.sol_text: Given: r = L/sqrt(2), so sin(theta) = r/L = 1/sqrt(2), therefore theta = 45°. For circular motion: T*sin(theta) = mv²/r and T*cos(theta) = mg. Dividing: tan(theta) = v²/(rg). Since tan(45°) = 1, we get v²/(rg) = 1, therefore v = sqrt(rg).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A bomb is dropped by a fighter plane flying horizontally. To an observer sitting in the plane, the trajectory of the bomb is a:
options: parabola in the direction of motion of plane
straight line vertically down the plane
parabola in a direction opposite of the motion of plane
questions.sol_text: Horizontal component of velocity of bomb equals to the velocity of plane. So, bomb and plane are in same vertical plane.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The magnitude of vectors OA, OB and OC in the given figure are equal. The direction of OA + OB - OC with x-axis will be:-
questions.sol_text: Given |OA| = |OB| = |OC| = ℓ. From the figure: OA = ℓ(cos30°i + sin30°j) = ℓ(sqrt(3)/2 i + 1/2 j). OB = ℓ(cos60°i + sin60°(-j)) = ℓ(1/2 i + sqrt(3)/2(-j)). OC = ℓ(cos45°(-i) + sin45°(i)) = ℓ(-1/sqrt(2) i + 1/sqrt(2) j). Computing OA + OB - OC: x-component = ℓ(sqrt(3)/2 + 1/2 + 1/sqrt(2)). y-component = ℓ(1/2 - sqrt(3)/2 - 1/sqrt(2)). Simplifying: x = (sqrt(3) + 1 + sqrt(2))/2 and y = (1 - sqrt(3) - sqrt(2))/2. Therefore tan(θ) = y/x = (1-sqrt(3)-sqrt(2))/(sqrt(3)+1+sqrt(2)) = (1-sqrt(3)-sqrt(2))/(1+sqrt(3)+sqrt(2)) after rationalizing.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The trajectory of a projectile in a vertical plane is y = alpha*x - beta*x^2, where alpha and beta are constants and x & y are respectively the horizontal and vertical distances of the projectile from the point of projection θ and the maximum height attained H are respectively given by:
questions.sol_text: From y = alpha*x - beta*x^2, taking dy/dx = alpha - 2*beta*x = 0 gives x = alpha/(2*beta). The maximum height is y_max = alpha * alpha/(2*beta) - beta * (alpha/(2*beta))^2 = alpha^2/(4*beta). The trajectory equation y = x*tan(theta) - g*x^2/(2*u^2*cos^2(theta)) is compared with the given equation. From dy/dx at x=0, we get tan(theta) = alpha, so theta = tan^(-1)(alpha). The maximum height H = alpha^2/(4*beta).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A particle is moving with uniform speed along the circumference of a circle of radius R under the action of a central fictitious force F which is inversely proportional to R^3. Its time period of revolution will be given by:
questions.sol_text: For circular motion, centripetal force F = mv^2/R. Given F ∝ 1/R^3, so F = k/R^3 where k is constant. Therefore mv^2/R = k/R^3, which gives v^2 = k/(mR^2), so v = sqrt(k/(mR^2)) = sqrt(k/m)/R. Time period T = 2πR/v = 2πR/(sqrt(k/m)/R) = 2πR^2/sqrt(k/m). Thus T ∝ R^2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A player kicks a football with an initial speed of 25 ms^(-1) at an angle of 45° from the ground. What are the maximum height and the time taken by the football to reach at the highest point during motion? (Take g = 10 ms^(-2))
questions.sol_text: For projectile motion: h_max = u^2 sin^2(theta) / (2g) = (25^2 × sin^2(45°)) / (2 × 10) = (625 × (1/sqrt(2))^2) / 20 = (625 × 0.5) / 20 = 15.625m. Time to reach maximum height: T = u sin(theta) / g = (25 × sin(45°)) / 10 = (25 × (1/sqrt(2))) / 10 = 1.77s

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The resultant of these forces OP, OQ, OR, OS and OT is approximately .... N [Take sqrt(3) = 1.7, sqrt(2) = 1.4. Given i and j unit vectors along x, y axis]
questions.sol_text: Calculate x-component (Fx): 10 × (sqrt(3)/2) + 20 × (1/2) + (20/sqrt(2)) - (15/2) - (15*sqrt(3)/2) = 9.25i. Calculate y-component (Fy): 15 × (1/2) + 20 × (sqrt(3)/2) + 10 × (1/2) - (15/sqrt(2)) - (20/sqrt(2)) = 5j. Resultant = 9.25i + 5j

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: If A, B, C, D are four points on a semi-circular arc with centre at 'O' such that |AB| = |BC| = |CD|, then which of the following is correct? Assertion A: AB + AC + AD = 4AO + OB + OC. Reason R: Polygon law of vector addition yields AB + BC + CD = AD = 2AO. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer.
options: A is not correct but R is correct.
A is correct but R is not correct.
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.sol_text: From the polygon law of vector addition, AB + BC + CD = AD. Since A and D are endpoints of the diameter, AD = 2AO. For the assertion, using vector addition: AB + AC + AD can be rewritten using the given equal segments and the semicircular geometry. The reason correctly applies the polygon law. Both statements are correct, but the reason explains the vector addition relationship used to derive the assertion.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A ball is thrown up with a certain velocity so that it reaches a height 'h'. Find the ratio of the two different times of the ball reaching h/3 in both the directions.
questions.sol_text: Given: h = u^2/(2g), u = sqrt(2gh). Ball reaches height h/3. Using S = ut + (1/2)at^2, we get h/3 = sqrt(2gh)t - (1/2)gt^2. Solving: 0 = t((9/2) - sqrt(2gh) + h/3). This gives two times t1 and t2. From the quadratic equation: t1 = (sqrt(2gh) - sqrt(4gh/3)) / g and t2 = (sqrt(2gh) + sqrt(4gh/3)) / g. Therefore, t1/t2 = (sqrt(2gh) - sqrt(4gh/3)) / (sqrt(2gh) + sqrt(4gh/3)) = (sqrt(3) - sqrt(2)) / (sqrt(3) + sqrt(2)).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Two forces (P + Q) and (P - Q) where P ⊥ Q, when act at an angle θ₁ to each other, the magnitude of their resultant is sqrt(3(P^2 + Q^2)), when they act at an angle θ₂, the magnitude of their resultant becomes sqrt(2(P^2 + Q^2)). This is possible only when θ₁ < θ₂. In the situation given above, θ₁ = 60° and θ₂ = 90°. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are false
Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false
Statement-I is false but Statement-II is true
questions.sol_text: Let x = P + Q = sqrt(P^2 + Q^2) and y = P - Q = sqrt(P^2 + Q^2). Then |x + y| = sqrt(x^2 + y^2 + 2xy) = sqrt(3(P^2 + Q^2)), which gives θ₁ = 60°. Using the same formula for θ₂ = 90°, we get the resultant as sqrt(2(P^2 + Q^2)). This confirms that θ₁ = 60° and θ₂ = 90° are consistent with the given conditions, making both statements true.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A helicopter is flying horizontally with a speed 'v' at an altitude 'h' has to drop a food packet for a man on the ground. What is the distance of helicopter from the man when the food packet is dropped?
questions.sol_text: The food packet falls from height h. Time to fall: h = (1/2)gt^2, so t = sqrt(2h/g). During this time, the packet moves horizontally with velocity v: x = vt = v*sqrt(2h/g). The distance of helicopter from man when packet is dropped is the straight-line distance: distance = sqrt(h^2 + x^2) = sqrt(h^2 + v^2*2h/g) = sqrt(2v^2h/g + h^2)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A swimmer can swim with velocity of 12 km/h in still water. Water flowing in a river has velocity 6 km/h. The direction with respect to the direction of flow of river water he should swim in order to reach the point on the other bank just opposite to his starting point is _________. (Round off to the Nearest Integer) (Find the angle in degrees)
questions.sol_text: Let u = swimmer's velocity in still water = 12 km/h, v = river flow velocity = 6 km/h. For the swimmer to reach directly opposite point, the net velocity should be perpendicular to the river flow. Using sin(theta) = u/v, we get sin(theta) = 6/12 = 1/2, so theta = 30 degrees. Total angle from direction of flow = 90 + 30 = 120 degrees.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The projectile motion of a particle of mass 5g is shown in the figure. The initial velocity of the projectile is 5*sqrt(2) m/s and air resistance is assumed to be negligible. The magnitude of change in momentum between the points A and B is x*10^-2 kg m/s. The value of x, to the nearest integer, is.................
questions.sol_text: Using the formula for change in momentum: |Δp| = 2mu*sin(θ) = 2 × 5 × 10^-3 × 5*sqrt(2) × 1/sqrt(2) = 5 × 10^-2 kg m/s. Therefore x = 5
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A person is swimming with a speed of 10 m/s at an angle of 120° with the flow and reaches to a point directly opposite on the other side of the river. The speed of the flow is 'x' m/s. The value of 'x' to the nearest integer is __________.
questions.sol_text: Given: Swimming speed v = 10 m/s, angle with flow = 120°. The angle from direction of flow θ = 90° + θ = 120°, so θ = 30°. For the person to reach directly opposite, the x-component of velocity (along flow direction) must be zero. Using sin(30°) = u/v, where u is the component along flow and v is swimming speed. sin(30°) = u/10, so 1/2 = u/10, therefore u = 5 m/s. Since the person reaches directly opposite, the flow speed x = 5 m/s.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Three particles P, Q and R are moving along the vectors A = i + j, B = j + k and C = -i + j respectively. They strike on point and start to move in different directions. Now particle P is moving normal to the plane which contains vector A and B. Similarly particle Q is moving normal to the plane which contains vector A and C. The angle between the direction of motion of P and Q is cos^(-1)(1/sqrt(x)). Then the value of x is ___.
questions.sol_text: Direction of motion of P: (i + j) × (j + k) = k - j + i = k - j + i. Direction of motion of Q: (i + j) × (-i + j) = 2k. cos(theta) = (a·b)/(ab) = 2/(2*sqrt(3)) = 1/sqrt(3) = 0 = cos^(-1)(1/sqrt(3)). Therefore x = 3.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: If P × Q = Q × P, the angle between P and Q is θ(0° < θ < 360°). The value of 'θ' will be ......
questions.sol_text: If angle between them is 180° then P · Q = -a·B = 0
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Two spherical balls having equal masses with radius of 5 cm each are thrown upwards along the same vertical direction at an interval of 3s with the same initial velocity of 35 m/s, then these balls collide at a height of ________ m. (Take g = 10 m/s²)
questions.sol_text: Let the first ball be thrown at t=0 and second ball at t=3s. For collision, y1 = y2. Using equation of motion: y1 = 35t - (1/2)×10×t² and y2 = 35(t-3) - (1/2)×10×(t-3)². Setting y1 = y2 and solving: 35t - 5t² = 35(t-3) - 5(t-3)², which simplifies to 35×3 = (5/2)×g(t+t-3)×3. This gives 105 = (10/2)×3×(2t-3), so t = 5s. Height y1 = 35×5 - (1/2)×10×5² = 175 - 125 = 50m.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A swimmer wants to cross a river from point A to point B. Line AB makes an angle of 30° with the flow of river. Magnitude of velocity of the swimmer is same as that of the river. The angle θ with the line AB should be _______, so that the swimmer reaches point B.
questions.sol_text: Given: |V_s| = |V_r| = v, angle between AB and river flow = 30°. The swimmer's velocity relative to ground must be along AB. Using vector addition: V_r = V_sr + V_r. For resultant to be along AB at angle 30° to river flow, with equal magnitudes of swimmer and river velocities, applying tan(30°) = v*sin(theta + 30°)/(v*cos(theta + 30°) + v). This gives sqrt(3)*sin(theta + 30°) = cos(theta + 30°) + 1, which simplifies to sin(theta) = 1/2, therefore theta = 30°.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A projectile is projected with velocity of 25 m/s at an angle θ with the horizontal. After t seconds its inclination with horizontal becomes zero. If R represents horizontal range of the projectile, the value of θ will be [use g = 10 m/s²]
questions.sol_text: At time t, vertical velocity becomes zero: vy = 25 sin(θ) - gt = 0, so t = (25 sin(θ))/g = (25 sin(θ))/10. Range R = (25²(2 sin(θ) cos(θ)))/g = (625 × 2 sin(θ) cos(θ))/10 = 125 sin(2θ)/2 = 50t cos(θ). From tan(θ) = (gt/25) × (50t/R) = (20t²)/R, we get θ = cot^(-1)[R/(20t²)]

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A ball is projected from the ground with a speed 15 ms^(-1) at an angle θ with horizontal so that its range and maximum height are equal, then tan θ will be equal to
questions.sol_text: For projectile motion: Range R = (u^2 sin(2θ))/g and Maximum Height H = (u^2 sin^2(θ))/(2g). Given R = H, so (u^2 sin(2θ))/g = (u^2 sin^2(θ))/(2g). Simplifying: sin(2θ) = sin^2(θ)/2. Using sin(2θ) = 2sin(θ)cos(θ): 2sin(θ)cos(θ) = sin^2(θ)/2. Dividing by sin(θ): 2cos(θ) = sin(θ)/2. Therefore tan(θ) = 4sin(θ)/sin(θ) = 4 × 1 = 4.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A person moved from A to B on a circular path as shown in figure. If the distance travelled by him is 60 m, then the magnitude of displacement would be (Given cos135° = -0.7)
questions.sol_text: Distance travelled = 60 m => Angle covered = 135°. Using Displacement = 2R sin(135°/2) = 2(60/135 × 180/pi)[(1-cos(135°))/2]^(1/2) = 2(80/pi)(0.85)^(1/2) ≈ 47 m

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Given below are two statements. One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R. Assertion A: Two identical balls A and B thrown with same velocity 'u' at two different angles with horizontal attained the same range R. If A and B reached the maximum height h1 and h2 respectively, then R = 4*sqrt(h1*h2). Reason R: Product of said heights. h1*h2 = (u^2*sin^2(theta))/(2g) * (u^2*cos^2(theta))/(2g). Choose the correct answer:
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.sol_text: h1 = u^2*sin^2(theta)/(2g), h2 = u^2*cos^2(theta)/(2g). Therefore, sqrt(h1*h2) = u^2*sin(theta)*cos(theta)/(2g) = R/4. Hence R = 4*sqrt(h1*h2). Both assertion and reason are true, and reason correctly explains assertion.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: For a particle in uniform circular motion, the acceleration a at any point P(R, θ) on the circular path of radius R is (when θ is measured from the positive x-axis and v is uniform speed)
questions.sol_text: In uniform circular motion, acceleration is centripetal, directed towards the center with magnitude v^2/R. The position vector of P is R(cos(θ)i + sin(θ)j). The acceleration points towards center (opposite direction), so a = -(v^2/R)cos(θ)i - (v^2/R)sin(θ)j

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A is a vector quantity such that |A| = non-zero constant. Which of the following expression is true for A?
questions.sol_text: A × A = |A| × |A| × sin(0°) = 0. The cross product of any vector with itself is always zero because the angle between a vector and itself is 0°, and sin(0°) = 0.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Which of the following relations is true for two unit vector A and B making an angle θ to each other?
questions.sol_text: For unit vectors A and B with angle θ between them: |A - B|^2 = |A|^2 + |B|^2 - 2|A||B|cos(θ) = 1 + 1 - 2cos(θ) = 2(1 - cos(θ)) = 2·2sin^2(θ/2), so |A - B| = 2sin(θ/2). Similarly, |A + B|^2 = 1 + 1 + 2cos(θ) = 2(1 + cos(θ)) = 2·2cos^2(θ/2), so |A + B| = 2cos(θ/2). Therefore, |A - B|/|A + B| = tan(θ/2), which gives |A - B| = |A + B| tan(θ/2).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Two projectiles are thrown with same initial velocity making an angle of 45° and 30° with the horizontal respectively. The ratio of their respective ranges will be
questions.sol_text: Range formula: R = u^2 sin(2θ) / g. For θ1 = 45°: R1 = u^2 sin(90°) / g = u^2 / g. For θ2 = 30°: R2 = u^2 sin(60°) / g = u^2 * sqrt(3)/2 / g. Ratio R1/R2 = sin(90°) / sin(60°) = 1 / (sqrt(3)/2) = 2/sqrt(3). Therefore R1 : R2 = 2 : sqrt(3)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Two projectiles thrown at 30° and 45° with the horizontal respectively, reach the maximum height in same time. The ratio of their initial velocities is:
questions.sol_text: Time to reach maximum height: ta = u sin(theta)/g. For same time to reach max height: u1 sin(30°)/g = u2 sin(45°)/g. Therefore: u1 sin(30°) = u2 sin(45°). u1 (1/2) = u2 (1/sqrt(2)). u1/u2 = (1/sqrt(2))/(1/2) = 2/sqrt(2) = sqrt(2)/1 = sqrt(2):1

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A body of mass 10 kg is projected at an angle of 45° with the horizontal. The trajectory of the body is observed to pass through a point (20, 10). If T is the time of flight, then its momentum vector, at time t = T/sqrt(2), is ________. [Take g = 10 m/s²]
questions.sol_text: Using trajectory equation y = x*tan(θ)(1 - x/R) with θ = 45°, point (20,10) gives R = 40 m. From R = u²sin(2θ)/g = 40, we get u = 20 m/s. Time of flight T = 2u*sin(θ)/g = 4/sqrt(2) s, so T/sqrt(2) = 2s. At t = 2s: vx = u*cos(45°) = 10√2 m/s, vy = u*sin(45°) - gt = 10√2 - 20 m/s. Momentum p = m*v = 10(10√2 i + (10√2 - 20)j) = 100√2 i + (100√2 - 200)j

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A projectile is launched at an angle 'alpha' with the horizontal with a velocity 20 ms^(-1). After 10s, its inclination with horizontal is 'beta'. The value of tan(beta) will be (g = 10 ms^(-2)).
questions.sol_text: Initial velocity components: V_x = 20cos(alpha), V_y = 20sin(alpha). After 10s: V_y = 20sin(alpha) - g*t = 20sin(alpha) - 10*10 = 20sin(alpha) - 100. V_x remains 20cos(alpha). tan(beta) = V_y/V_x = (20sin(alpha) - 100)/(20cos(alpha)) = sin(alpha)/cos(alpha) - 100/(20cos(alpha)) = tan(alpha) - 5sec(alpha).

questions.text: Motion of a particle in x-y plane is described by a set of following equations x = 4sin(pi/2 - ωt) m and y = 4sin(ωt) m. The path of the particle will be
questions.sol_text: Given: x = 4sin(pi/2 - ωt) = 4cos(ωt) and y = 4sin(ωt). Squaring both equations: x^2 = 16cos^2(ωt) and y^2 = 16sin^2(ωt). Adding: x^2 + y^2 = 16cos^2(ωt) + 16sin^2(ωt) = 16(cos^2(ωt) + sin^2(ωt)) = 16. Therefore x^2 + y^2 = 4^2, which is the equation of a circle with radius 4 m. The particle is moving in circular motion.

questions.text: A ball is projected with kinetic energy E, at an angle of 60° to the horizontal. The kinetic energy of this ball at the highest point of its flight will become:
questions.sol_text: Initial kinetic energy E = (1/2)mu². At the highest point of trajectory, only horizontal component of velocity remains. The horizontal velocity component is V = u cos(60°) = u/2. Therefore, kinetic energy at topmost point = (1/2)m(u/2)² = (1/2)m(u²/4) = (1/4)mu² = E/4

questions.text: Two vectors A and B have equal magnitudes. If magnitude of A + B is equal to two times the magnitude of A - B then the angle between A and B will be -
questions.sol_text: Let |A| = |B| = A. Given |A + B| = 2|A - B|. Squaring both sides: A^2 + A^2 + 2A^2 cos(theta) = 2(A^2 + A^2 - 2A^2 cos(theta)). Simplifying: 2A^2 + 2A^2 cos(theta) = 2(2A^2 - 2A^2 cos(theta)). This gives: 2A^2 + 2A^2 cos(theta) = 4A^2 - 4A^2 cos(theta). Therefore: 5 cos(theta) = 3, so cos(theta) = 3/5. Thus theta = cos^(-1)(3/5).

questions.sol_text: The component of vector A along vector B is given by A cos(theta) = (A·B)/|B|. Calculate A·B = (2)(1) + (3)(2) + (-1)(2) = 2 + 6 - 2 = 6. Calculate |B| = sqrt(1^2 + 2^2 + 2^2) = sqrt(1 + 4 + 4) = sqrt(9) = 3. Therefore, component = 6/3 = 2 m.

questions.sol_text: Given trajectory: y = 5x(1 - x) = 5x - 5x^2. The standard trajectory equation is y = x*tan(θ) - (g*x^2)/(2*v^2). Comparing coefficients: tan(θ) = 5 and g/(2*v^2) = 5. Since initial horizontal velocity u_x = 1 (unit vector i), we have tan(θ) = u_y/u_x = u_y/1. Therefore u_y = 5.

questions.text: A fighter jet is flying horizontally at a certain altitude with a speed of 200 m/s. When it passes directly overhead an anti-aircraft gun, a bullet is fired from the gun, at an angle θ with the horizontal, to hit the jet. If the bullet speed is 400 m/s, the value of θ will be ____°.
questions.sol_text: For the bullet to hit the jet, the horizontal component of bullet's velocity must equal the jet's velocity. Let bullet speed = 400 m/s, jet speed = 200 m/s. Horizontal component of bullet: 400 cos(θ) = 200. Therefore, cos(θ) = 200/400 = 1/2. Thus, θ = 60°.

questions.text: A ball of mass m is thrown vertically upward. Another ball of mass 2m is thrown at an angle θ with the vertical. Both the balls stay in air for the same period of time. The ratio of the heights attained by the two balls respectively is 1/x. The value of x is ___.
questions.sol_text:
For ball 1 (mass m, thrown vertically upward with initial velocity u1): Time in air t1 = 2u1/g, Maximum height H1 = u1^2/(2g)

For ball 2 (mass 2m, thrown at angle θ with vertical with initial velocity u2): The vertical component of velocity is u2*sin(θ). Time in air t2 = 2u2*sin(θ)/g, Maximum height H2 = (u2*sin(θ))^2/(2g)

Since both stay in air for same time: t1 = t2
2u1/g = 2u2*sin(θ)/g
Therefore: u1 = u2*sin(θ)

Ratio of heights: H1/H2 = [u1^2/(2g)] / [(u2*sin(θ))^2/(2g)] = u1^2 / (u2*sin(θ))^2 = (u2*sin(θ))^2 / (u2*sin(θ))^2 = 1

Given H1/H2 = 1/x, therefore x = 1

questions.text: A body is projected from the ground at an angle of 45° with the horizontal. Its velocity after 2 s is 20 ms^(-1). The maximum height reached by the body during its motion is _______ m. (use g = 10 ms^(-2))
questions.sol_text: Initial velocity components: u_cos(45°) = horizontal component, u_sin(45°) - gt = vertical component at t=2s. Given v = 20 m/s at t=2s, so v^2 = (u_cos(45°))^2 + (u_sin(45°) - gt)^2 = 400. Solving these equations: u = 20√2 m/s. Maximum height H = u^2 sin^2(45°) / (2g) = (20√2)^2 × (1/2) / 20 = 800 × 0.5 / 20 = 20 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A child stands on the edge of the cliff 10 m above the ground and throws a stone horizontally with an initial speed of 5 ms^(-1). Neglecting the air resistance, the speed with which the stone hits the ground will be ___ ms^(-1) (given, g = 10 ms^(-2)).
questions.sol_text:
Given:
- Initial horizontal velocity, u = 5 m/s
- Height of cliff, h = 10 m
- Acceleration due to gravity, g = 10 m/s^2
- Stone is thrown horizontally

When the stone is thrown horizontally, it has only horizontal component of velocity initially. As it falls, it gains vertical velocity component.

Final velocity when stone hits ground:
v = sqrt(u^2 + 2gh)

where u is the initial horizontal velocity (which remains constant throughout the motion).

Substituting the values:
v = sqrt((5)^2 + 2 × 10 × 10)
v = sqrt(25 + 200)
v = sqrt(225)
v = 15 m/s

questions.text: For a body projected at an angle with the horizontal from the ground, choose the correct statement.
options: The horizontal component of velocity is zero at the highest point.
The vertical component of momentum is maximum at the highest point
Gravitational potential energy is maximum at the highest point
The Kinetic Energy (K.E.) is zero at the highest point of projectile motion.
questions.sol_text:
At highest point KE = (1/2)mv^2 cos^2(theta) ≠ 0

horizontal momentum = mv cos(theta) ≠ 0
vertical momentum = 0
PE = mgh (Max at maximum height)

Statement (1): FALSE - The horizontal component of velocity is v cos(theta) ≠ 0 at the highest point. Only the vertical component of velocity is zero.

Statement (2): FALSE - The vertical component of momentum is zero at the highest point, not maximum. It is maximum at the ground level.

Statement (3): TRUE - Gravitational potential energy PE = mgh is maximum at the highest point since h is maximum there.

Statement (4): FALSE - The kinetic energy at the highest point is KE = (1/2)mv^2 cos^2(theta) ≠ 0 because the horizontal velocity component v cos(theta) still exists.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A body of mass 200 g is tied to a spring of spring constant 12.5 N/m, while the other end of spring is fixed at point O. If the body moves about O in a circular path on a smooth horizontal surface with constant angular speed 5 rad/s. Then the ratio of extension in the spring to its natural length will be:
questions.sol_text:
For circular motion on a smooth horizontal surface, the spring force provides the centripetal force.

Let l = natural length of spring
Let x = extension in the spring
Then radius of circular path r = l + x

The spring force is: F_s = kx

For circular motion, centripetal force required is: F_c = mω²(l + x)

Equating spring force to centripetal force:
kx = mω²(l + x)

Substituting values:
m = 200 g = 0.2 kg
k = 12.5 N/m
ω = 5 rad/s

12.5x = 0.2 × (5)² × (l + x)
12.5x = 0.2 × 25 × (l + x)
12.5x = 5(l + x)
12.5x = 5l + 5x
12.5x - 5x = 5l
7.5x = 5l
(7.5/5)x = l
(3/2)x = l

Therefore:
x/l = 2/3

The ratio of extension to natural length is x : l = 2 : 3

P and Q are perpendicular

⇒ (1)(4) + (2m)(2) + (m)(m) = 0
⇒ 4 + 4m + m^2 = 0
⇒ m^2 + 4m + 4 = 0
⇒ (m + 2)^2 = 0
⇒ m = -2

questions.text: An object moves at a constant speed along a circular path in a horizontal plane with centre at the origin. When the object is at x = +2 m, its velocity is -4 j m/s. The object's velocity (v) and acceleration (a) at x = -2 m will be
questions.sol_text:
Given: Object moves at constant speed along circular path with centre at origin. At x = +2 m, velocity v = -4j m/s

From the diagram, the circular path has radius R = 2 m.

Speed of object: |v| = |-4j| = 4 m/s

Centripetal acceleration magnitude: a = v^2/R = 16/2 = 8 m/s^2

At position x = +2 m:
- Position vector: r = 2i m
- Velocity: v = -4j m/s (perpendicular to radius, pointing downward)
- The velocity is tangent to the circle

At position x = -2 m:
- Position vector: r = -2i m (diametrically opposite)
- The object is at the opposite end of the diameter
- Velocity direction is perpendicular to the new radius, so v = 4j m/s (pointing upward)
- Acceleration is centripetal, pointing toward center, so a = 8i m/s^2 (pointing toward origin in +i direction)

Therefore: v = 4j m/s, a = 8i m/s^2

questions.text: A body is moving with constant speed, in a circle of radius 10 m. The body completes one revolution in 4 s. At the end of 3rd second, the displacement of body (in m) from its starting point is:
questions.sol_text:
r = 10 m
T = 4 sec
At t = 3 s, the body has completed 3/4 of the circle.

Angle covered in 3 seconds:
θ = (3/4) × 2π = (3π/2) radians

Starting point: t = 0 (at top of circle)
Position at t = 3 s: The body has moved 3/4 of the circumference, which corresponds to an angle of 270° or 3π/2 radians from the starting point.

Using the diagram, if we place the starting point at the top (t = 0):
- At t = 1 s: 1/4 revolution (90°) - position at right
- At t = 2 s: 1/2 revolution (180°) - position at bottom
- At t = 3 s: 3/4 revolution (270°) - position at left

The displacement is the straight-line distance from starting point (top) to final position (left side).

Using the circle geometry, when the body is at 3/4 revolution from the starting point:
The two radii form a 270° angle, or equivalently, a 90° angle from the opposite direction.

Displacement d = sqrt(r^2 + r^2 - 2r^2×cos(270°))
Or more directly: d = sqrt(r^2 + r^2) = r√2
d = 10√2 m

T = 2u sin(30°)/g = 2u × (1/2)/g = u/g

questions.text: A car is moving on a circular path of radius 600 m such that the magnitudes of the tangential acceleration and centripetal acceleration are equal. The time taken by the car to complete first quarter of revolution, if it is moving with an initial speed of 54 km/hr is t(1 - e^(-pi/2)) s. The value of t is ____.
questions.sol_text:
Given: Radius R = 600 m, initial speed v_0 = 54 km/hr = 15 m/s

Condition: Tangential acceleration = Centripetal acceleration
|dv/dt| = v^2/R

Therefore: dv/dt = v^2/R

Separating variables:
dv/v = (v/R) * ds

Integrating:
dv/v = ds/R
ln(v)|_15^v = s/R
ln(v/15) = s/R
v = 15e^(s/R)

Since v = ds/dt:
ds/dt = 15e^(s/R)
dt = (1/15)e^(-s/R) ds

For quarter revolution, s = (pi*R)/2 = (pi*600)/2 = 300*pi

Integrating from t = 0 to t = Delta(t) and s = 0 to s = 300*pi:
Delta(t) = ∫[0 to 300*pi] (1/15)e^(-s/R) ds
= (1/15) * [-R*e^(-s/R)]|_0^(300*pi)
= (1/15) * R * [1 - e^(-300*pi/600)]
= (1/15) * 600 * [1 - e^(-pi/2)]
= 40[1 - e^(-pi/2)] seconds

Comparing with t(1 - e^(-pi/2)) s:
t = 40

⟹ θ₂ = 30°

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The speed of a swimmer is 4 km h^(-1) in still water. If the swimmer makes his strokes normal to the flow of river of width 1 km, he reaches a point 750 m down the stream on the opposite bank. The speed of the river water is __________ km h^(-1)
questions.sol_text:
Let speed of river water = v_0

Drift = v_0 × Δt ... (1)

& Δt = 1/4 h ... (2)

The swimmer swims perpendicular to the flow (normal to the flow), so the swimmer's velocity perpendicular to the river is 4 km/h.

Time taken to cross the river of width 1 km:
Δt = width / speed perpendicular to flow
Δt = 1 / 4 = 1/4 h

Drift (distance moved downstream) = 750 m = 0.75 km

Using equation (1):
0.75 = v_0 × (1/4)

v_0 = 0.75 × 4
v_0 = 3 km/h

questions.text: A non-conducting ring of mass m and radius R has uniformly distributed charge Q. It is placed on a smooth horizontal surface. questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A particle moving in a circle of radius R with uniform speed takes time T to complete one revolution. If this particle is projected with the same speed at an angle θ to the horizontal, the maximum height attained by it is equal to 4R. The angle of projection θ is then given by:
questions.sol_text: From circular motion, T = 2π*R/v, so v = 2π*R/T. For projectile motion, H_max = v^2*sin^2(θ)/(2g) = 4R. Therefore v^2*sin^2(θ) = 8gR. Substituting v: (2π*R/T)^2*sin^2(θ) = 8gR, which gives sin^2(θ) = 8gR*T^2/(4π^2*R^2) = 2gT^2/(π^2*R). Thus θ = sin^(-1)[(2gT^2)/(π^2*R)]^(1/2)

However, from the solution shown, if we consider the geometry where P and S form a right angle at the center (90 degrees), then using the chord formula: Displacement = R*sqrt(2) = 2*sqrt(2) = sqrt(8) km, where R = 2 km is the radius.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The angle of projection for a projectile to have same horizontal range and maximum height is:
questions.sol_text: For a projectile, horizontal range R = u^2 sin(2θ)/g and maximum height H = u^2 sin^2(θ)/(2g). Given R = H: u^2 sin(2θ)/g = u^2 sin^2(θ)/(2g). Simplifying: 2 sin(2θ) = sin^2(θ). Using sin(2θ) = 2sin(θ)cos(θ): 4sin(θ)cos(θ) = sin^2(θ). Dividing by sin(θ): 4cos(θ) = sin(θ). Therefore tan(θ) = 4, giving θ = tan^(-1)(4).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A ball suspended by a thread swings in a vertical plane so that its magnitude of acceleration in the extreme position and lowest position are equal. The angle (θ) of thread deflection in the extreme position will be:
questions.sol_text: At extreme position: a1 = g sin(θ). At mean position: a2 = v^2/l where v^2 = 2g(1 - cos(θ)). Given a1 = a2, so g sin(θ) = 2g(1 - cos(θ)). This gives sin(θ) = 2(1 - cos(θ)). Using tan(θ/2) = 1/2, we get θ = 2 tan^(-1)(1/2).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: If the radius of curvature of the path of two particles of same mass are in the ratio 3:4, then in order to have constant centripetal force, their velocities will be in the ratio of:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Projectiles A and B are thrown at angles of 45° and 60° with vertical respectively from top of a 400 m high tower. If their ranges and times of flight are same, the ratio of their speeds of projection vA : vB is: [Take g = 10 m/s²]
questions.sol_text: For same time of flight, vertical component of velocity of projection must be same. vA sin(45°) = vB sin(30°). Therefore, vA/vB = sin(30°)/sin(45°) = (1/2)/(1/sqrt(2)) = sqrt(2)/2 × 2 = 1/sqrt(2) = 1 : sqrt(2)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: If two vectors A and B having equal magnitude R are inclined at an angle θ, then

questions.text: Two forces F₁ and F₂ are acting on a body. One force has magnitude thrice that of the other force and the resultant of the two forces is equal to the force of larger magnitude. The angle between F₁ and F₂ is cos^(-1)(1/n). The value of |n| is ____.
questions.sol_text: Let |F₁| = F and |F₂| = 3F. The resultant F_R = 3F (equal to larger force). Using the law of cosines: F_R^2 = F₁^2 + F₂^2 + 2F₁F₂cos(θ). Substituting: (3F)^2 = F^2 + (3F)^2 + 2(F)(3F)cos(θ). This gives: 9F^2 = F^2 + 9F^2 + 6F^2cos(θ). Simplifying: 0 = F^2 + 6F^2cos(θ), so cos(θ) = -1/6. Therefore θ = cos^(-1)(-1/6), which means n = -6, and |n| = 6.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The maximum height reached by a projectile is 64 m. If the initial velocity is halved, the new maximum height of the projectile is _____ m.
questions.sol_text: Maximum height formula: H_max = u^2 sin^2(theta) / (2g). When initial velocity u is halved to u/2, the new height H_2max = (u/2)^2 sin^2(theta) / (2g) = u^2 sin^2(theta) / (4 × 2g) = (1/4) × u^2 sin^2(theta) / (2g) = H_max / 4. Since H_max = 64 m, H_2max = 64/4 = 16 m.

questions.text: For three vectors A = (-xi - 6j - 2k), B = (-i + 4j + 3k) and C = (-8i - j + 3k), if A · (B × C) = 0, then value of x is ____.
questions.sol_text: Calculate B × C using determinant form: B × C = |i  j  k; -1  4  3; -8  -1  3| = 15i - 21j + 33k. Then A · (B × C) = (-xi - 6j - 2k) · (15i - 21j + 33k) = -15x + 126 - 66 = 0. Solving: -15x + 60 = 0, so 15x = 60, therefore x = 4.

questions.text: A body of mass M thrown horizontally with velocity v from the top of the tower of height H touches the ground at a distance of 100m from the foot of the tower. A body of mass 2M thrown at a velocity v/2 from the top of the tower of height 4H will touch the ground at a distance of ........m.
questions.sol_text: For first body: H = (1/2)gt1^2, so t1 = sqrt(2H/g). Horizontal distance: 100 = v*t1 = v*sqrt(2H/g). For second body: 4H = (1/2)gt2^2, so t2 = sqrt(2(4H)/g) = sqrt(8H/g) = 2*sqrt(2H/g). Horizontal distance: x = (v/2)*t2 = (v/2)*2*sqrt(2H/g) = v*sqrt(2H/g) = 100m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Three vectors OP, OQ and OR each of magnitude A are acting as shown in figure. The resultant of the three vectors is A*sqrt(x). The value of x is ____.
questions.sol_text: From the figure, vector OQ is at 90° from OP, and OR is at 45° below OP. Setting up coordinates with OP along positive x-axis: OP = A*i, OQ = A*j, OR = A*cos(-45°)*i + A*sin(-45°)*j = (A/sqrt(2))*i - (A/sqrt(2))*j. Resultant R = (A + A/sqrt(2))*i + (A - A/sqrt(2))*j. Magnitude |R| = sqrt((A + A/sqrt(2))^2 + (A - A/sqrt(2))^2) = sqrt(A^2 + 2*A^2/sqrt(2) + A^2/2 + A^2 - 2*A^2/sqrt(2) + A^2/2) = sqrt(3*A^2) = A*sqrt(3). Therefore x = 3.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The resultant of two vectors A and B is perpendicular to A and its magnitude is half that of B. The angle between vectors A and B is ...........
questions.sol_text: Let R be the resultant of vectors A and B. Given: R is perpendicular to A, |R| = |B|/2. Since R ⊥ A, we have R · A = 0. Using (A + B) · A = 0, we get A² + B · A = 0. From the magnitude: |A + B|² = (|B|/2)², which gives A² + 2A·B + B² = B²/4. This leads to A·B = -A²/2. Combining these equations and solving: cos(θ) = B·A/(|B||A|) = -B/2, so θ = 150°.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: If a and b makes an angle cos^(-1)(5/9) with each other, then |a + b| = sqrt(2)|a - b| for |a| = n|b|. The integer value of n is ......
questions.sol_text: Given: cos(θ) = 5/9, so (a·b)/(ab) = 5/9. From |a + b| = sqrt(2)|a - b|, squaring both sides: a^2 + b^2 + 2a·b = 2(a^2 + b^2 - 2a·b). This gives 6a·b = a^2 + b^2. Substituting a = nb: 6 × (5/9) × nb^2 = n^2b^2 + b^2. Simplifying: (10/3)nb^2 = n^2b^2 + b^2. Dividing by b^2: (10/3)n = n^2 + 1, which gives 3n^2 - 10n + 3 = 0. Solving: n = 1/3 or n = 3. Since n must be an integer, n = 3.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.text: A particle starts from origin at t = 0 with a velocity 5i m/s and moves in x-y plane under action of a force which produces a constant acceleration of (3i + 2j) m/s². If the x-coordinate of the particle at that instant is 84 m, then the speed of the particle at this time is sqrt(alpha) m/s. The value of alpha is ______.
questions.sol_text: Using kinematic equation: x = v₀t + (1/2)at² → 84 = 5t + (1/2)(3)t² → 84 = 5t + 1.5t² → 3t² + 10t - 168 = 0. Solving: t = 6 s. Velocity at t = 6s: v = v₀ + at = 5i + 6(3i + 2j) = 5i + 18i + 12j = 23i + 12j. Speed: v = sqrt(23² + 12²) = sqrt(529 + 144) = sqrt(673). Therefore alpha = 673.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A particle is moving in a circle of radius 50 cm in such a way that at any instant the normal and tangential components of its acceleration are equal. If its speed at t = 0 is 4 m/s, the time taken to complete the first revolution will be (1/alpha)[1 - e^(-2*pi)] s, where alpha = ________.
questions.sol_text: Given: radius r = 50 cm = 0.5 m, v0 = 4 m/s, normal acceleration = tangential acceleration. Normal acceleration = v^2/r, tangential acceleration = dv/dt. Setting equal: v^2/r = dv/dt. Rearranging: dt = (r*dv)/v^2. For one complete revolution, s = 2*pi*r. From v^2/r = dv/dt and integrating with s = integral(v*dt): ln(v/v0) = s/r = 2*pi. Thus v = v0*e^(2*pi). Also: t/r = 1/v0 - 1/(v0*e^(2*pi)). Simplifying: t = (r/v0)[1 - e^(-2*pi)] = (1/alpha)[1 - e^(-2*pi)]. With r = 0.5 m and v0 = 4 m/s: alpha = v0/r = 4/0.5 = 8.

questions.text: Two projectiles are fired from ground with same initial speeds from same point at angles (45° + α) and (45° - α) with horizontal direction. The ratio of their times of flights is
questions.sol_text: Time of flight T = (2u sin θ)/g. For projectile 1 at angle (45° + α): T1 = 2u sin(45° + α)/g. For projectile 2 at angle (45° - α): T2 = 2u sin(45° - α)/g. Ratio T1/T2 = sin(45° + α)/sin(45° - α). Expanding: sin(45° + α) = (cos α + sin α)/sqrt(2) and sin(45° - α) = (cos α - sin α)/sqrt(2). Therefore T1/T2 = (cos α + sin α)/(cos α - sin α) = (1 + tan α)/(1 - tan α).

questions.text: A particle is projected at an angle of 30° from horizontal at a speed of 60 m/s. The height traversed by the particle in the first second is h0 and height traversed in the last second, before it reaches the maximum height, is h1. The ratio h0 : h1 is ______. [Take, g = 10 m/s^2]
questions.sol_text:
Initial vertical component of velocity: uy = 60 sin(30°) = 60 × (1/2) = 30 m/s

Height traversed in the first second (h0):
S1 = uy × t - (1/2) × g × t^2
S1 = 30 × 1 - (1/2) × 10 × 1^2 = 30 - 5 = 25 m

Time to reach maximum height:
t_max = uy/g = 30/10 = 3 seconds

Height traversed in the last second before reaching maximum height (during 3rd second, from t=2 to t=3):
Using S_n = uy + (g/2)(2n - 1) where n is the nth second (but with upward as positive and g as negative in this context)

Alternatively, distance in 3rd second:
S3 = 30 + (-10/2) × (2 × 3 - 1) = 30 - 5 × 5 = 30 - 25 = 5 m

Or using S = ut + (1/2)at^2:
Displacement in first 3 seconds: s3 = 30(3) - (1/2)(10)(3)^2 = 90 - 45 = 45 m
Displacement in first 2 seconds: s2 = 30(2) - (1/2)(10)(2)^2 = 60 - 20 = 40 m
h1 = s3 - s2 = 45 - 40 = 5 m

Ratio:
h0/h1 = 25/5 = 5

questions.text: A particle is projected with velocity u so that its horizontal range is three times the maximum height attained by it. The horizontal range of the projectile is given as mu^2/(25g), where value of n is: (g is acceleration due to gravity)

questions.text: The angle of projection of a particle is measured from the vertical axis as φ and the maximum height reached by the particle is h_m. Here h_m as function of φ can be presented as

Graph 3: h_m decreases monotonically from maximum at φ = 0° to zero at φ = 90°

A boat, moving with speed of 36 km/h in still water, is made to travel one-round trip (bank to bank of the river). Minimum time taken by the boat for this journey and also the displacement along the river bank are ____ and ____ respectively.
questions.sol_text:
Given:
River width = 200 m
River velocity v_R = 18 km/h = 5 m/s
Boat velocity in still water v_BW = 36 km/h = 10 m/s

Minimum time:
For a round trip (bank to bank), the boat must travel perpendicular to the river flow to minimize displacement along the bank.
The effective velocity perpendicular to the river = v_BW = 10 m/s

For one-way journey:
t_min = 200/10 = 20 sec

For round trip:
t_min = 2 × 20 = 40 sec

Displacement along river bank:
During the journey perpendicular to the bank (to minimize displacement), the river current carries the boat downstream.
In time t = 40 sec, displacement along river = v_R × t = 5 × 40 = 200 m

Therefore, minimum time = 40 s and displacement along river bank = 200 m

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A projectile is thrown upward at an angle 60° with the horizontal. The speed of the projectile is 20 m/s when its direction of motion is 45° with the horizontal. The initial speed of the projectile is ____ m/s.
questions.sol_text:
Let the initial speed of the projectile be u, thrown at angle 60° with the horizontal.

Initial velocity components:
u_x = u*cos(60°) = u/2
u_y = u*sin(60°) = u*sqrt(3)/2

At any time t during the motion:
v_x = u*cos(60°) = u/2 (remains constant, no horizontal acceleration)
v_y = u*sin(60°) - g*t = u*sqrt(3)/2 - g*t

At the point where the direction of motion is 45° with the horizontal:
tan(45°) = |v_y|/v_x = 1

Therefore: |v_y| = v_x

Also, the speed at this point is 20 m/s:
v^2 = v_x^2 + v_y^2 = 20^2 = 400

Since |v_y| = v_x and v_x^2 + v_y^2 = 400:
v_x^2 + v_x^2 = 400
2*v_x^2 = 400
v_x^2 = 200
v_x = sqrt(200) = 10*sqrt(2)

From v_x = u*cos(60°) = u/2:
u/2 = 10*sqrt(2)
u = 20*sqrt(2) m/s

Alternatively, using the given diagram notation:
u*cos(60°) = 20/sqrt(2)
u*(1/2) = 20/sqrt(2)
u = 40/sqrt(2) = 40*sqrt(2)/2 = 20*sqrt(2) m/s
